```{r load-libraries}
library(igraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(knitr)
library(scales)
library(pROC)
library(irlba)
library(Matrix)
library(purrr)

set.seed(42)

OUT_DIR <- "../plots"
dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Unified color palette (seaborn deep)
# Updated color palette: More vibrant but professionally balanced
COLOR_PRIMARY   <- "#2A52BE" # Cerulean Blue
COLOR_SECONDARY <- "#E63946" # Soft Crimson
COLOR_ACCENT    <- "#2A9D8F" # Persian Green
COLOR_NEUTRAL   <- "#457B9D" # Steel Blue
PALETTE_DEEP    <- c(COLOR_PRIMARY, COLOR_SECONDARY, COLOR_ACCENT, 
                     "#F4A261", "#8338EC", "#FFBE0B")

# Re-defined theme_network with a premium aesthetic
# Re-defined theme_network with premium aesthetic + histogram-specific spacing
theme_network <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    # Titles: Stronger hierarchy
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, color = "#1A1A1A", margin = margin(b = 30)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "#666666", margin = margin(b = 20)),
    plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8, color = "#999999", margin = margin(t = 20)),
    
    # NEW: Specific spacing for Histogram Labels
    # Increased 'r' (right) margin for Y to move "Count" away from the grid
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13, color = "#333333", margin = margin(r = 20)),
    # Increased 't' (top) margin for X to move "Degree" away from numbers
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, color = "#333333", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    
    # Background: Soft "Paper" feel instead of stark white
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
    
    # Grids: Subtle hairlines to let the data (nodes/edges/bars) pop
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#FFFFFF", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    
    # Legend: Clean and centered at the top
    legend.position   = "top",
    legend.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    
    # Margin: Overall plot breathing room
    plot.margin = margin(30, 30, 30, 30)
  )
```

# Introduction

This report presents a comprehensive statistical analysis of the MUSAE GitHub developer social network. The dataset comprises 37,700 GitHub users connected by 289,003 mutual-follower edges. Each developer carries a binary attribute (`ml_target`) indicating whether they are primarily a machine-learning developer (1) or not (0).

We follow the analytical pipeline from Kolaczyk and Csardi's *Statistical Analysis of Network Data with R*, progressing through seven chapters:

1. **Introduction** -- dataset description and research questions.
2. **Manipulating Network Data** -- loading, constructing, and validating the graph.
3. **Visualizing Network Data** -- practical layouts for large networks.
4. **Descriptive Analysis** -- degree, centrality, cohesion, community structure, assortativity.
5. **Mathematical Models** -- comparing the observed graph to Erdos--Renyi and configuration model baselines.
6. **Statistical Models** -- dyad-level logistic regression, stochastic block model, and spectral embedding.
7. **Network Topology Inference** -- link prediction via heuristic scores and stacked classification.

The central questions are: What structural properties characterize the GitHub developer network? Does it exhibit small-world or scale-free behavior? Can local topology predict missing links?

# Manipulating Network Data

## Loading the Data

```{r ch2-load-data}
edges_df  <- read_csv("../musae_git_edges.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
target_df <- read_csv("../musae_git_target.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Constructing the Graph

```{r ch2-create-graph}
g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges_df, vertices = target_df, directed = FALSE)
g <- simplify(g)
```

```{r ch2-overview}
overview <- tibble(
  Nodes        = vcount(g),
  Edges        = ecount(g),
  Density      = graph.density(g),
  Simple       = is.simple(g),
  Connected    = is.connected(g)
)
kable(overview, digits = 6, caption = "Graph overview")
```

## Data Quality Checks

```{r ch2-quality}
quality <- tibble(
  `Self-loops`     = sum(which_loop(g)),
  `Multi-edges`    = sum(which_multiple(g)),
  `Isolated nodes` = sum(degree(g) == 0)
)
kable(quality, caption = "Data quality checks")
```

## Attribute Summary

```{r ch2-ml-target}
ml_counts <- target_df %>%
  count(ml_target) %>%
  mutate(fraction = n / sum(n))
kable(ml_counts, digits = 4, caption = "ml\\_target class balance")
write_csv(ml_counts, file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch2_ml_target_balance.csv"))

```

## Top Hub Nodes

```{r ch2-top-hubs}
deg_all <- degree(g)
top_hubs <- tibble(
  id        = as.integer(V(g)$name),
  name      = V(g)$name,
  degree    = deg_all,
  ml_target = as.integer(V(g)$ml_target)
) %>%
  slice_max(degree, n = 15)

kable(top_hubs, caption = "Top 15 nodes by degree")
write_csv(top_hubs, file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch2_top_hubs.csv"))
```

# Visualizing Network Data

With 37,700 nodes, full-graph visualization is impractical. We apply three strategies: a high k-core subgraph with spring layout, an ego-centric view of the top hub, and a community-colored subgraph.

## K-Core Subgraph with Spring Layout

```{r ch3-kcore-extract}
core_num <- coreness(g)
core_threshold <- 20
g_core <- induced_subgraph(g, V(g)[core_num >= core_threshold])
cat("High-core subgraph:", vcount(g_core), "nodes,", ecount(g_core), "edges\n")
```

```{r ch3-spring-layout, fig.width=9, fig.height=9}
set.seed(42)
lay_fr <- layout_with_fr(g_core, niter = 500)

V(g_core)$color <- ifelse(as.integer(V(g_core)$ml_target) == 0,
                           COLOR_PRIMARY, COLOR_SECONDARY)
V(g_core)$size  <- 2 + sqrt(degree(g_core)) * 0.4

pdf(file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch3_high_core_spring.pdf"), width = 10, height = 10)
plot(g_core,
     layout       = lay_fr,
     vertex.label = NA,
     vertex.frame.color = NA,
     edge.color   = adjustcolor(COLOR_NEUTRAL, alpha.f = 0.15),
     edge.width   = 0.3,
     main         = sprintf("High k-core (k >= %d) subgraph: %d nodes",
                            core_threshold, vcount(g_core)))
legend("bottomleft",
       legend = c("ml_target = 0", "ml_target = 1"),
       col    = c(COLOR_PRIMARY, COLOR_SECONDARY),
       pch    = 19, pt.cex = 1.5, bty = "n")
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Ego Network of the Top Hub

```{r ch3-ego-network, fig.width=9, fig.height=9}
hub_idx <- which.max(deg_all)
g_ego   <- make_ego_graph(g, order = 1, nodes = hub_idx)[[1]]

V(g_ego)$color <- ifelse(as.integer(V(g_ego)$ml_target) == 0,
                          COLOR_PRIMARY, COLOR_SECONDARY)
V(g_ego)$size  <- ifelse(V(g_ego)$name == V(g)$name[hub_idx], 8, 2)

set.seed(42)
lay_ego <- layout_with_kk(g_ego)

pdf(file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch3_ego_hub.pdf"), width = 10, height = 10)
plot(g_ego,
     layout       = lay_ego,
     vertex.label = NA,
     vertex.frame.color = NA,
     edge.color   = adjustcolor(COLOR_NEUTRAL, alpha.f = 0.1),
     edge.width   = 0.2,
     main         = sprintf("Ego network of top hub (degree = %d)", deg_all[hub_idx]))
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Community-Colored Subgraph

```{r ch3-community-vis, fig.width=9, fig.height=9}
comm_core <- cluster_fast_greedy(g_core)
mem_core  <- membership(comm_core)
V(g_core)$color <- PALETTE_DEEP[(mem_core - 1) %% length(PALETTE_DEEP) + 1]

pdf(file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch3_community_colored.pdf"), width = 10, height = 10)
plot(g_core,
     layout       = lay_fr,
     vertex.label = NA,
     vertex.frame.color = NA,
     vertex.size  = 2 + sqrt(degree(g_core)) * 0.4,
     edge.color   = adjustcolor(COLOR_NEUTRAL, alpha.f = 0.15),
     edge.width   = 0.3,
     main         = sprintf("Community structure (fast-greedy, %d communities)",
                            length(comm_core)))
invisible(dev.off())
```

# Descriptive Analysis of Network Characteristics

## Degree Distribution

```{r ch4-degree-stats}
deg <- degree(g)
deg_summary <- tibble(
  Mean   = mean(deg),
  SD     = sd(deg),
  Median = median(deg),
  Min    = min(deg),
  Max    = max(deg),
  P90    = quantile(deg, 0.90),
  P99    = quantile(deg, 0.99)
)
kable(deg_summary, digits = 2, caption = "Degree distribution summary")
write_csv(deg_summary, file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch4_degree_stats.csv"))
```

```{r ch4-degree-ccdf, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
deg_sorted <- sort(deg)
n_nodes    <- length(deg_sorted)
ccdf_vals  <- 1 - seq_len(n_nodes) / n_nodes

deg_df <- tibble(degree = deg_sorted, ccdf = pmax(ccdf_vals, 1e-8))

p_ccdf <- ggplot(deg_df, aes(x = degree, y = ccdf)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.6, color = COLOR_PRIMARY) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Degree (log)", y = "CCDF (log)",
       title = "Degree Distribution: Log-Log CCDF") +
  theme_network
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "loglog_degree_distribution.pdf"), p_ccdf, width = 7, height = 5)
p_ccdf
```

```{r ch4-degree-hist, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
p_hist <- ggplot(tibble(degree = deg), aes(x = degree)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 900, fill = COLOR_PRIMARY, color = "#FFFFFF", linewidth = 0.2) +
  labs(x = "Degree (linear scale)", y = "Count",
       title = "Linear Degree Histogram") +
  theme_network
p_hist <- p_hist +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1000))
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "linear_degree_histogram.pdf"), p_hist, width = 7, height = 4)
p_hist
```

```{r ch4-degree-hist, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
p_hist <- ggplot(tibble(degree = deg), aes(x = degree)) +
  # Using a small binwidth or specific bins for log scales is usually cleaner
  geom_histogram(bins = 90, fill = COLOR_PRIMARY, color = "#FFFFFF", linewidth = 0.2) +
  # Set limits here; 1 is the usual start for degree distributions

  labs(x = "Degree (log scale)",

       title = "Logiarithmic Degree Histogram") +

ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "log_log_degree_histogram.pdf"), p_hist, width = 7, height = 4)

```

## Centrality Measures

```{r ch4-centrality, cache=TRUE}
deg_cent     <- degree(g, normalized = TRUE)
close_cent   <- closeness(g, normalized = TRUE)
between_cent <- betweenness(g, normalized = TRUE)
eigen_cent   <- eigen_centrality(g)$vector
pr_cent      <- page_rank(g, damping = 0.85)$vector
```

```{r ch4-centrality-table}
centrality_df <- tibble(
  id               = as.integer(V(g)$name),
  name             = V(g)$name,
  ml_target        = as.integer(V(g)$ml_target),
  degree           = deg,
  degree_centrality = deg_cent,
  closeness        = close_cent,
  betweenness      = between_cent,
  eigenvector      = eigen_cent,
  pagerank         = pr_cent
)

centrality_df %>%
  select(degree_centrality, closeness, betweenness, eigenvector, pagerank) %>%
  summary() %>%
  kable(caption = "Centrality measure summaries")
```

```{r ch4-top-pagerank, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
top20_pr <- centrality_df %>%
  slice_max(pagerank, n = 20) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(id, ":", substr(name, 1, 12)),
         ml_fac = factor(ml_target, levels = c(0, 1)))

p_pr <- ggplot(top20_pr, aes(x = reorder(label, pagerank), y = pagerank, fill = ml_fac)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("0" = COLOR_PRIMARY, "1" = COLOR_SECONDARY),
                    labels = c("0" = "Non-ML", "1" = "ML")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PageRank", fill = "ml_target",
       title = "Top 20 Nodes by PageRank") +
  theme_network
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch4_top_pagerank.pdf"), p_pr, width = 8, height = 6)
p_pr

write_csv(top20_pr %>% select(-label, -ml_fac),
          file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch4_top_centrality.csv"))
```

```{r ch4-centrality-corr, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
cor_mat <- centrality_df %>%
  select(degree_centrality, closeness, betweenness, eigenvector, pagerank) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

cor_mat
```

```{r}
cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat)) %>%
  rename(Var1 = Var1, Var2 = Var2, Correlation = Freq)

p_corr <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Correlation)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = COLOR_SECONDARY, mid = "white", high = COLOR_PRIMARY,
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Centrality Measure Correlations") +
  theme_network +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.title = element_blank())
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "centrality_correlation.pdf"), p_corr, width = 6, height = 5)
p_corr
```

```{r}
# 1. Reorder the matrix (Optional but recommended for visual patterns)
# This groups similar centrality measures together
dd <- as.dist((1 - cor_mat) / 2)
hc <- hclust(dd)
cor_mat_ordered <- cor_mat[hc$order, hc$order]

# 2. Convert to long format and remove the upper triangle
# This makes the plot much cleaner and less "busy"
cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat_ordered)) %>%
  rename(Var1 = Var1, Var2 = Var2, Correlation = Freq) %>%
  mutate(Correlation = round(Correlation, 2))

# Optional: Hide the upper triangle for a professional look
cor_long <- cor_long %>%
  filter(as.numeric(Var1) >= as.numeric(Var2))

# 3. Create the improved plot
p_corr <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Correlation)) +
  # Use a subtle border for the tiles
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  # Conditional text coloring: use white text for dark backgrounds, black for light
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Correlation), 
                color = abs(Correlation) > 0.7), 
            size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Keep your specific palette
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = COLOR_SECONDARY, mid = "white", high = COLOR_PRIMARY,
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1),
                       name = "Pearson\nCorr.") +
  # Text color logic: White text on dark tiles, grey on light tiles
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "white", "FALSE" = "grey20")) +
  labs(title = "Centrality Measure Correlations",
       subtitle = "Variables ordered by hierarchical clustering") +
  theme_network + 
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), # Remove grid for a cleaner look
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 10)
  ) +
  coord_fixed() # Ensures tiles are perfectly square

# Save and Display
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "centrality_correlation_refined.pdf"), p_corr, width = 7, height = 6)
p_corr
```

## Transitivity and Clustering

```{r ch4-transitivity}
trans_global    <- transitivity(g, type = "global")
trans_local_avg <- transitivity(g, type = "localaverage")
trans_local     <- transitivity(g, type = "local")

trans_tbl <- tibble(
  `Global transitivity`        = trans_global,
  `Mean local clustering coef.` = trans_local_avg
)
kable(trans_tbl, digits = 4, caption = "Transitivity summary")
```
```{r}
length(articulation.points(g))
vertex.connectivity(g)
edge.connectivity(g)
```


```{r ch4-local-clustering, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
cc_df <- tibble(cc = trans_local[!is.nan(trans_local)])

p_cc <- ggplot(cc_df, aes(x = cc)) +local 
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = COLOR_PRIMARY, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  labs(x = "Local clustering coefficient", y = "Count",
       title = "Distribution of Local Clustering Coefficients") +
```

```{r}
  geom_col(fill = COLOR_PRIMARY) +
```

## Assortativity

```{r ch4-assortativity}
assort_deg <- assortativity_degree(g)
assort_ml  <- assortativity_nominal(g, types = as.integer(V(g)$ml_target) + 1)

assort_tbl <- tibble(
  Measure = c("Degree assortativity", "ml_target assortativity (nominal)"),
  Value   = c(assort_deg, assort_ml)
)
kable(assort_tbl, digits = 4, caption = "Assortativity coefficients")
```

The negative degree assortativity ($r \approx -0.075$) indicates that high-degree hubs tend to connect to low-degree nodes (disassortative mixing). The positive ml\_target assortativity ($r \approx 0.378$) reveals strong homophily: developers of the same type preferentially connect.

## Cohesion Metrics

```{r ch4-cohesion, cache=TRUE}
n_comp    <- components(g)$no
diam_val  <- diameter(g, directed = FALSE)
vert_conn <- vertex_connectivity(g)
edge_conn <- edge_connectivity(g)

approx_avg_path <- function(graph, n_samples = 500) {
  nodes <- sample(V(graph), min(n_samples, vcount(graph)))
  dists <- distances(graph, v = nodes)
  mean(dists[dists < Inf & dists > 0])
}
avg_path <- approx_avg_path(g)

cohesion_tbl <- tibble(
  Components           = n_comp,
  Diameter             = diam_val,
  `Vertex connectivity` = vert_conn,
  `Edge connectivity`   = edge_conn,
  `Approx. avg path length` = round(avg_path, 3)
)
kable(cohesion_tbl, caption = "Cohesion metrics")
```

```{r ch4-save-global}
global_metrics <- tibble(
```

# Mathematical Models for Network Graphs

We compare the observed network against classical random graph baselines to assess which features are structurally noteworthy.

## Erdos--Renyi Model

```{r ch5-er, cache=TRUE}
n_g <- vcount(g)
m_g <- ecount(g)
p_er <- (2 * m_g) / (n_g * (n_g - 1))

n_reps <- 5
er_results <- map_dfr(1:n_reps, function(rep) {
  set.seed(42 + rep)
  g_er <- sample_gnp(n_g, p_er)
  gc_er <- largest_component(g_er)
  tibble(
    model       = "Erdos-Renyi",
    replicate   = rep,
    nodes       = vcount(g_er),
    edges       = ecount(g_er),
    transitivity = transitivity(g_er, type = "global"),
    avg_path    = approx_avg_path(gc_er, n_samples = 300)
  )
})
```

## Configuration Model

```{r ch5-config, cache=TRUE}
deg_seq <- degree(g)
config_results <- map_dfr(1:n_reps, function(rep) {
  set.seed(42 + 100 + rep)
  g_cfg <- tryCatch(
    sample_degseq(deg_seq, method = "simple"),
    error = function(e) sample_degseq(deg_seq, method = "vl")
  )
  g_cfg <- simplify(g_cfg)
  gc_cfg <- largest_component(g_cfg)
  tibble(
    model       = "Configuration",
    replicate   = rep,
    nodes       = vcount(g_cfg),
    edges       = ecount(g_cfg),
    transitivity = transitivity(g_cfg, type = "global"),
    avg_path    = approx_avg_path(gc_cfg, n_samples = 300)
  )
})
```

```{r ch5-comparison}
kable(model_cmp, digits = 4, caption = "Observed vs. random graph baselines")
write_csv(model_cmp, file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch5_model_comparison.csv"))
```

## Small-World Assessment

```{r ch5-small-world}
er_trans_mean <- mean(er_results$transitivity)
er_apl_mean   <- mean(er_results$avg_path)
sigma <- (trans_global / er_trans_mean) / (avg_path / er_apl_mean)
cat("Small-world sigma:", round(sigma, 2), "\n")
```

A sigma value much greater than 1 confirms small-world structure: the network has far higher clustering than an ER graph while maintaining comparable path lengths.

# Statistical Models for Network Graphs

## Dyad-Level Logistic Regression (ERGM Proxy)

Full ERGMs are computationally infeasible on a 37,700-node graph. We instead fit a dyad-level logistic regression on sampled edges and non-edges, using local structural features as predictors.

```{r ch6-link-features}
compute_link_features <- function(pairs_mat, graph) {
  n_pairs <- nrow(pairs_mat)
  cn <- jc <- aa <- pa <- same_tgt <- numeric(n_pairs)
  deg_g   <- degree(graph)
  ml_vec  <- as.integer(V(graph)$ml_target)

  for (i in seq_len(n_pairs)) {
    u <- pairs_mat[i, 1]
    v <- pairs_mat[i, 2]
    nu <- neighbors(graph, u)
    nv <- neighbors(graph, v)
    common <- intersect(nu, nv)

    cn[i] <- length(common)
    union_size <- length(union(nu, nv))
    jc[i] <- if (union_size > 0) cn[i] / union_size else 0

    aa_score <- 0
    for (w in common) {
      dw <- deg_g[w]
      if (dw > 1) aa_score <- aa_score + 1 / log(dw)
    }
    aa[i] <- aa_score
    pa[i] <- deg_g[u] * deg_g[v]
    same_tgt[i] <- as.integer(ml_vec[u] == ml_vec[v])
  }

  tibble(cn = cn, jaccard = jc, adamic_adar = aa,
         pref_attach = pa, same_target = same_tgt)
}
```


```{r ch6-sample-nonedges}
sample_non_edges <- function(graph, n_samples) {
  n <- vcount(graph)
  A <- as_adjacency_matrix(graph, sparse = TRUE)
  pairs <- matrix(NA_integer_, nrow = n_samples, ncol = 2)
  count <- 0
  while (count < n_samples) {
    u <- sample.int(n, 1)
    v <- sample.int(n, 1)
    if (u != v && A[u, v] == 0) {
      count <- count + 1
      pairs[count, ] <- c(u, v)
    }
  }
  pairs
}
```

```{r ch6-dyad-logistic, cache=TRUE}
set.seed(42)
all_el    <- as_edgelist(g, names = FALSE)
pos_idx   <- sample(nrow(all_el), min(60000, nrow(all_el)))
pos_pairs <- all_el[pos_idx, , drop = FALSE]
neg_pairs <- sample_non_edges(g, nrow(pos_pairs))

X_pos <- compute_link_features(pos_pairs, g)
X_neg <- compute_link_features(neg_pairs, g)

dyad_df <- bind_rows(
  X_pos %>% mutate(y = 1),
  X_neg %>% mutate(y = 0)
)
dyad_df$log_pref_attach <- log1p(dyad_df$pref_attach)

train_idx <- sample(nrow(dyad_df), floor(0.75 * nrow(dyad_df)))
train <- dyad_df[train_idx, ]
test  <- dyad_df[-train_idx, ]

model_dyad <- glm(y ~ cn + jaccard + adamic_adar + same_target + log_pref_attach,
                  data = train, family = binomial)

dyad_probs <- predict(model_dyad, test, type = "response")
dyad_auc   <- as.numeric(auc(roc(test$y, dyad_probs, quiet = TRUE)))
cat("Dyad logistic AUC:", round(dyad_auc, 4), "\n")
```

```{r ch6-dyad-coefs}
coef_df <- tibble(
  feature     = names(coef(model_dyad))[-1],
  coefficient = coef(model_dyad)[-1]
) %>% arrange(desc(abs(coefficient)))

kable(coef_df, digits = 4, caption = "Dyad logistic regression coefficients")
write_csv(coef_df, file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch6_dyad_logistic_coefficients.csv"))
```

## Stochastic Block Model

Using the binary `ml_target` attribute as the block assignment, we compute the within-block and between-block edge probabilities.

```{r ch6-block-model}
ml_vec <- as.integer(V(g)$ml_target)
n0 <- sum(ml_vec == 0)
n1 <- sum(ml_vec == 1)

el <- as_edgelist(g, names = FALSE)
types_u <- ml_vec[el[, 1]]
types_v <- ml_vec[el[, 2]]

count_00 <- sum(types_u == 0 & types_v == 0)
count_11 <- sum(types_u == 1 & types_v == 1)
count_01 <- ecount(g) - count_00 - count_11

block_probs <- tibble(
  block           = c("0-0", "0-1", "1-1"),
  observed_edges  = c(count_00, count_01, count_11),
  possible_pairs  = c(choose(n0, 2), n0 * n1, choose(n1, 2)),
  edge_probability = observed_edges / possible_pairs
)

kable(block_probs, digits = 6, caption = "Block model edge probabilities")
write_csv(block_probs, file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch6_block_model_probabilities.csv"))
```

```{r ch6-spectral, cache=TRUE}
svd_result <- irlba(A_sparse, nv = 2)
latent_xy  <- svd_result$u %*% diag(svd_result$d[1:2])
```

```{r ch6-latent-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
latent_sample <- tibble(

p_latent <- ggplot(latent_sample, aes(x = x, y = y, color = ml_fac)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +

                     labels = c("0" = "Non-ML", "1" = "ML")) +

p_latent
```

```{r ch6-latent-classify}
latent_df <- tibble(x = latent_xy[, 1], y = latent_xy[, 2], target = ml_vec)
set.seed(42)
lat_train_idx <- sample(nrow(latent_df), floor(0.75 * nrow(latent_df)))
```

# Network Topology Inference (Link Prediction)

We evaluate the ability of local structural features to predict missing edges. We hold out 20% of edges as test positives and sample an equal number of non-edges as test negatives.

## Train/Test Split

```{r ch7-split, cache=TRUE}
set.seed(42)
all_edges <- as_edgelist(g, names = FALSE)
n_edges   <- nrow(all_edges)
test_edge_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_edges), floor(0.2 * n_edges))

test_pos   <- all_edges[test_edge_idx, , drop = FALSE]
train_el   <- all_edges[-test_edge_idx, , drop = FALSE]

g_train <- delete_edges(g, test_edge_idx)
cat("Training graph:", vcount(g_train), "nodes,", ecount(g_train), "edges\n")
cat("Test positives:", nrow(test_pos), "\n")
```

```{r ch7-negatives, cache=TRUE}
test_neg <- sample_non_edges(g, nrow(test_pos))
cat("Test negatives:", nrow(test_neg), "\n")
```

## Compute Link Prediction Features

```{r ch7-features, cache=TRUE}
n_train_lp   <- min(60000, nrow(train_el))
train_pos_lp <- train_el[sample(nrow(train_el), n_train_lp), , drop = FALSE]
train_neg_lp <- sample_non_edges(g, n_train_lp)

X_train_lp <- bind_rows(
  compute_link_features(train_pos_lp, g_train) %>% mutate(y = 1),
  compute_link_features(train_neg_lp, g_train) %>% mutate(y = 0)
)

X_test_lp <- bind_rows(
  compute_link_features(test_pos, g_train) %>% mutate(y = 1),
  compute_link_features(test_neg, g_train) %>% mutate(y = 0)
)
```

## Individual Heuristic AUCs

```{r ch7-individual-auc}
heuristic_aucs <- tibble(
  method = c("Common Neighbors", "Jaccard", "Adamic-Adar",
             "Preferential Attachment", "Same ml_target"),
  auc = c(
    as.numeric(auc(roc(X_test_lp$y, X_test_lp$cn, quiet = TRUE))),
    as.numeric(auc(roc(X_test_lp$y, X_test_lp$jaccard, quiet = TRUE))),
    as.numeric(auc(roc(X_test_lp$y, X_test_lp$adamic_adar, quiet = TRUE))),
    as.numeric(auc(roc(X_test_lp$y, X_test_lp$pref_attach, quiet = TRUE))),
    as.numeric(auc(roc(X_test_lp$y, X_test_lp$same_target, quiet = TRUE)))
  )
)
kable(heuristic_aucs %>% arrange(desc(auc)), digits = 4,
      caption = "AUC for individual link prediction heuristics")
```

## Stacked Logistic Regression

```{r ch7-stacked}
model_stack <- glm(y ~ cn + jaccard + adamic_adar + pref_attach + same_target,
                   data = X_train_lp, family = binomial)
stack_probs <- predict(model_stack, X_test_lp, type = "response")
stack_auc   <- as.numeric(auc(roc(X_test_lp$y, stack_probs, quiet = TRUE)))
cat("Stacked logistic AUC:", round(stack_auc, 4), "\n")
```

## ROC Curve Comparison

```{r ch7-roc, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
plot_roc <- function(roc_obj, label) {
  tibble(fpr = 1 - roc_obj$specificities,
         tpr = roc_obj$sensitivities,
         method = label)
}

roc_stack <- roc(X_test_lp$y, stack_probs, quiet = TRUE)
roc_cn    <- roc(X_test_lp$y, X_test_lp$cn, quiet = TRUE)
roc_aa    <- roc(X_test_lp$y, X_test_lp$adamic_adar, quiet = TRUE)
roc_pa    <- roc(X_test_lp$y, X_test_lp$pref_attach, quiet = TRUE)

roc_all <- bind_rows(
  plot_roc(roc_stack, sprintf("Stacked LR (AUC=%.3f)", stack_auc)),
  plot_roc(roc_cn,    sprintf("Common Neighbors (AUC=%.3f)", as.numeric(auc(roc_cn)))),
  plot_roc(roc_aa,    sprintf("Adamic-Adar (AUC=%.3f)", as.numeric(auc(roc_aa)))),
  plot_roc(roc_pa,    sprintf("Pref. Attach. (AUC=%.3f)", as.numeric(auc(roc_pa))))
)

p_roc <- ggplot(roc_all, aes(x = fpr, y = tpr, color = method)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = COLOR_NEUTRAL) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(COLOR_PRIMARY, COLOR_SECONDARY,
                                COLOR_ACCENT, "#DD8452")) +
  labs(x = "False Positive Rate", y = "True Positive Rate",
       title = "Link Prediction: ROC Curve Comparison", color = "Method") +
  theme_network +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.65, 0.25))
ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch7_link_prediction_roc.pdf"), p_roc, width = 8, height = 6)
p_roc
```

```{r ch7-auc-bar, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
all_aucs <- bind_rows(
  heuristic_aucs,
  tibble(method = "Stacked Logistic", auc = stack_auc)
) %>% arrange(desc(auc))

p_auc <- ggplot(all_aucs, aes(x = reorder(method, auc), y = auc)) +
  geom_col(fill = COLOR_PRIMARY) +

  labs(x = NULL, y = "AUC", title = "Link Prediction AUC Comparison") +

p_auc

write_csv(all_aucs, file.path(OUT_DIR, "ch7_link_prediction_auc.csv"))
```

# Conclusion

This analysis reveals several key properties of the GitHub developer social network:

- **Scale-free structure**: The degree distribution follows a heavy-tailed power law, with a small number of hubs accumulating thousands of connections.
- **Small-world properties**: The network exhibits far higher clustering than an Erdos--Renyi random graph while maintaining short average path lengths ($\sigma \gg 1$).
- **Strong homophily**: The positive ml\_target assortativity and the stochastic block model confirm that developers of the same type connect preferentially.
- **Effective link prediction**: Combining local heuristics (common neighbors, Adamic--Adar, preferential attachment) in a stacked logistic regression achieves strong AUC, with preferential attachment being the most powerful single predictor.
